core_obligations: Use the locally closed immersion parameterising the triviality of the module to express the hypothesis as bijectivity of that immersion.
Conclude the immersion is an isomorphism because the base is reduced, and read off the trivialising module.

proof_roadmap.step: Recall the locally closed immersion parameterising the triviality locus.
Use the fibre hypothesis to see it is bijective.
Conclude it is an isomorphism over a reduced base.

difficulty_reason: For a flat proper finitely presented family whose structure sheaf pushes forward to the structure sheaf of the base, stably under base change, a finite locally free module that is trivial on every fibre is pulled back from the base when the base is reduced. The proof uses the diagonal representability result to obtain a locally closed immersion parameterising the triviality locus, observes that the hypothesis makes it bijective, and then concludes it is an isomorphism because the base is reduced. Combining the locally closed immersion with bijectivity and reducedness is the content. Retained author proof at lines 9326-9331.
